subagent_reports.topic: Discovery opportunity scout: archive delta reconciliation

sources.label: Proposal and problem statement
sources.summary: Defines required missing/identical/conflicting reconciliation, archive-owned recovery, preserved evidence, stale versions/docs, and production-shaped regression scope.

sources.label: Existing-bundle terminal bypass
sources.summary: Already-archived bundles route directly to metadata reconciliation; existing bundles for non-archived changes synthesize success with empty spec/doc updates instead of reapplying or verifying deltas.

sources.label: Retry reconciler
sources.summary: Existing retry path reconciles release-gate and Phase 9 metadata only; phase9=skip returns immediate no-op success.

sources.label: Delta semantics
sources.summary: Add rejects every duplicate ID without identical-content classification; modify shallow-merges desired fields without precondition or prior-value evidence.

sources.label: Delta schema
sources.summary: Modify deltas contain target_id plus desired changes, but no expected preimage/base fingerprint; this limits safe historical conflict discrimination.

sources.label: Archive write ordering
sources.summary: Capabilities are applied and written one-by-one; docs are generated separately; errors accumulate, allowing partial projection before bundle handling.

sources.label: Archive authority
sources.summary: Archived change.json is written first as durable authority and hash-bound to terminal summary, preserving accepted deltas as canonical retry input.

sources.label: Current split-brain coverage
sources.summary: Live Temporal test proves release-gate and phase9_status recovery with an existing bundle, but does not assert spec delta, version, or generated-doc reconciliation.

sources.label: Temporal idempotency guidance
sources.summary: Temporal documents that Activities can execute more than once after ambiguous completion and should make external side effects idempotent.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Five bounded candidates, sorted by payoff/risk. (1) auto-adopt: route every existing-bundle no-op and status-repair terminal path through one archive-owned reconciliation postcondition before success; evidence shows current bypasses in change.ts and archive-gate.ts. (2) auto-adopt: add a read-only whole-change preflight classifying each delta as missing, identical, or conflict before any write; apply only after all semantic conflicts pass, while retaining retry for crash-partial writes. (3) inconclusive: define modification conflict authority. Current modify deltas lack preimage/base fingerprints, so desired postimage mismatch alone cannot distinguish an unapplied historical value from later conflicting law; future deltas should carry structural preconditions, while recovery of the already-shipped parent needs an evidence-backed baseline source selected during design. (4) auto-adopt: make reconciliation success cover requirement content, expected capability version, generated doc projection, archive bundle authority, and terminal status—not requirement IDs or status alone. (5) auto-adopt: extend production-shaped tests across partial prior application, identical add, missing add/modify, conflicting law, phase9 run/skip, and direct/PR retry; current live test checks metadata only. Existing pattern has a MAJOR deviation from the proposal invariant because terminal paths can report success without proving global spec projection.

validation.notes: Proposal direction is sound and four low-risk opportunities can be incorporated during agreement/design. Modification-conflict discrimination remains unresolved because archived modify deltas do not encode prior-value/preimage evidence.

tradeoffs: Whole-change preflight adds reads and comparison code but prevents avoidable semantic partial writes.
Rechecking full postconditions on every terminal retry costs bounded I/O but removes status-only trust.
Adding precondition fingerprints improves future conflict safety but changes the public delta contract and requires compatibility handling for historical bundles.
Multi-file writes cannot be made truly atomic with simple filesystem renames across all artifacts; deterministic idempotent reconciliation is simpler than introducing a transaction subsystem.

alternatives_considered.option: Trust archived status plus bundle existence
alternatives_considered.rationale: Current production incident and source paths show these markers can coexist with missing global law.
A marker can diverge from spec files and generated docs after partial writes; derived content reconciliation is stronger.

alternatives_considered.option: Derive retry truth from archived change.json plus current projections
alternatives_considered.rationale: Reuses existing durable authority and keeps archive as sole writer; requires explicit precondition strategy for ambiguous historical modifies.

alternatives_considered.option: Introduce a general transactional spec store
alternatives_considered.rationale: Broader than approved scope; whole-change preflight plus idempotent per-artifact reconciliation is simpler.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Adopt candidates 1, 2, 4, and 5 into discovery agreement/design. Route candidate 3 as an explicit design decision: define baseline/precondition evidence for historical modify recovery before authorizing overwrite; fail closed when that evidence cannot distinguish missing application from conflict.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Use archived change.json as retry input, require a single shared end-to-end reconciliation check before every terminal/no-op/status-repair success, preflight all deltas before writes, and test the observed partial-application sequence. Do not implement historical modify overwrite until baseline authority is explicit.

documents.proposal:
# Proposal: Fix archive delta reconciliation

## Why

`fixWorkflowReliabilityDefects` shipped and archived, but archive retry left accepted spec deltas unapplied. The archive bundle and release state say complete while global spec law remains incomplete.

### Agreed Facts

- Five added requirements remain absent from global specs.
- The `rq-TDD013evp` modification remains unapplied.
- `rq-subagentReports24` already exists and must remain single-copy.
- Capability versions and generated docs remain stale.
- The failure followed a Phase 9 conflict, later merge, then terminal archive no-op.

### Desired Outcome

Archived-change state and global spec law agree. Recovery restores the parent change's accepted deltas without duplicating existing law, corrupting conflicting law, or weakening archive ownership of global spec writes.

### Prior Decisions

- Track repair under fast-follow `fixArchiveDeltaReconciliation`.
- Preserve the archived parent and its release evidence.
- Keep archive as the sole global-spec writer.

### Rejected Approaches

- Direct manual global-spec edits as final architecture.
- Purging or rewriting the archived parent bundle.
- Reopening or falsifying the parent release state.
- Treating terminal archive status alone as proof of delta reconciliation.

### Open Questions

- Exact failure boundary and canonical retry behavior.
- Required reconciliation invariant across spec projection, bundle, merge, release, and archive status.
- Safest recovery path for already-shipped affected archives.

## What Changes

- Archive completion reflects whether every declared accepted delta is represented in global spec law.
- Recovery handles partial prior application without silent loss or duplicate law.
- The archived parent's missing accepted spec changes are restored through the archive-owned lifecycle.
- Conflicting existing law remains visible and blocks unsafe reconciliation.

## User Outcomes

- Maintainers can trust that an archived change's accepted spec deltas are present in global specs.
- Maintainers can retry interrupted archive work without losing already accepted law or creating duplicate requirements.
- Maintainers receive a clear failure when current global law conflicts with archived intent.
- Readers see capability versions and generated documentation consistent with repaired global specs.

## Affected Code

- `plugin/src/archive/archive.ts` and `plugin/src/archive/delta.ts`.
- `plugin/src/tools/change.ts`, `plugin/src/tools/change/archive-gate.ts`, and archive timeout/recovery surfaces.
- `adv_change_status_repair` and batch `adv_archive_repair action=reconcile` terminal-projection paths.
- Phase 9 unit tests, archive delta tests, and live Temporal integration tests.
- `.adv/specs/advance-meta`, `.adv/specs/advance-workflow`, `.adv/specs/subagent-reports`, `.adv/specs/tdd-contract`, and generated spec docs.

## Related Repositories

- Current `Advance` repository only.
- No cross-repository interface change identified.

## Constraints

- Archive remains sole global-spec writer.
- Preserve archived parent bundle and shipped release evidence.
- Preserve fail-closed handling for non-identical requirement conflicts.
- Avoid direct manual global-spec repair as final architecture.
- Maintain Temporal replay and crash-recovery safety.

## Impact

- Archive/release reliability for changes carrying spec deltas.
- Global specification correctness and generated documentation consistency.
- Recovery behavior for already-shipped archives with incomplete spec projection.

## Context

Fast-follow from archived change `fixWorkflowReliabilityDefects`. Current global versions remain `advance-meta` 1.28.0, `advance-workflow` 1.30.0, `subagent-reports` 1.7.3, and `tdd-contract` 1.7.1.

## Scope

### In Scope

- Diagnose archive sequencing and retry behavior that allowed terminal state with incomplete global spec projection.
- Define and enforce archive delta-reconciliation truth before terminal/no-op success.
- Cover normal archive, existing-bundle retry, archived no-op retry, `phase9=skip`, timeout retry, single status repair, and batch terminal repair surfaces.
- Handle identical prior application, missing application, and conflicting application safely.
- Restore all accepted missing parent deltas through canonical archive-owned behavior.
- Update affected generated spec documentation and capability versions.
- Add production-shaped regression coverage for observed interruption/retry sequence.

### Out of Scope

- Unrelated archive branch/worktree cleanup behavior.
- General redesign of Temporal persistence or seven-gate lifecycle.
- Purging, reopening, or rewriting unrelated archived changes.
- New product behavior beyond reliable archive delta reconciliation.
- Cross-repository release orchestration changes.

### Must Not

- Mark reconciliation successful from archive status alone.
- Duplicate an already-present identical requirement.
- Overwrite non-identical conflicting global law silently.
- Bypass archive ownership with an untracked manual spec edit.
- Weaken release evidence, gate sequencing, or replay safety.

## Discovery Agenda

- Trace exact ordering among delta application, bundle writing, Phase 9 finalization, release completion, archived status, and retry no-op checks.
- Define durable proof and equality for add and modify reconciliation.
- Compare current split-brain tests with production sequence that lost five additions and one modification.
- Check direct/PR and all terminal repair surfaces.
- Determine safe recovery for historical modify deltas without masking later law.

# Discovery Findings

## Skills Considered

# Design

## Architecture

Archive delta projection uses one archive-owned **Plan → Apply → Prove → Finalize** pipeline across first archive, retry, terminal verification, Temporal projection, and approved historical repair.

1. Plan strict deltas against authoritative specs in memory.
2. Apply only proven-safe missing projection in a validated change worktree.
3. Prove requirement content, capability version, docs, committed manifest, and immutable released commit.
4. Permit terminal state only after typed proof receipt.

Bundle existence, IDs, workflow status, and unverified markers never constitute proof.

## Canonical projection

One codec owns canonical serialization and SHA-256 for specs, requirements, delta sets, documents, manifests, seed state, and receipts. It uses authoritative passthrough `SpecSchema`/`RequirementSchema`, preserving and hashing valid extension fields; strict `DeltaSchema` and manifest schemas reject malformed authority.

Operations classify as `missing`, `identical`, `conflicting`, or `unverified`. Missing work applies once; identical state preserves bytes/version; conflict/unverified fails closed except the exact add-only preserve-current disposition below.

Bundles carry strict `spec-projection.json`. Immutable proof reads the committed manifest from one pinned SHA, binds it to external evidence and all accepted delta IDs, then reads specs/docs from that SHA.

## Worktree and writer serialization

Tracked writes target only validated `change/{id}` worktrees:

- `.adv/specs/{capability}/spec.json`
- `docs/specs/{capability}.md`
- `.adv/archive/{bundle}/...`

All archive projection writers—normal archive, existing-bundle active retry, and historical repair—use one shared cooperative archive-projection file lock stored under the repository Git common directory, outside tracked worktree files. Lock acquisition occurs before loading seed HEAD/specs and is held through planning, all writes, and readback. `finally` always releases it.

Approved historical execute also requires `expectedSeedHeadSha` and `expectedSeedProjectionSha256` from its reviewed dry-run. Under lock it re-resolves HEAD and canonical seed map; any mismatch fails before writes. Immediately before first write it repeats HEAD/seed digest checks. Atomic per-file writes plus lock and final readback provide bounded crash/retry safety; partial safe writes converge to the same fixed point.

Finalization stages only explicit archive-owned paths. Existing-bundle retry reuses evidence, applies missing work under the same lock, commits manifest/spec/docs, and skips repeated cleanup. Released/archived retry, timeout guidance, and status repairs are spec-read-only and require immutable proof.

## Temporal terminal path

New terminal histories carry typed `ArchiveProjectionProofReceipt` with change ID, manifest digest, full commit SHA, verified status/timestamp. `archiveChangeActivity` uses non-mutating `verify_summary`; `store.changes.save` refuses accepted-delta terminal state without receipt and routes receipt-bearing state through `archiveRequestedSignal`.

`wf.patched("archive-projection-reconciler-v1")` preserves old activity mutation only for replay of recorded histories. New histories require receipt. Replay fixtures cover both branches.

## Historical repair

`adv_archive_repair action=reconcile_deltas` requires trusted clean repair worktree. Dry-run is read-only. Execute requires approval, evidence, recovery reason, reviewed seed HEAD/digest, and typed conflict dispositions.

Algorithm:

1. Dry-run pins HEAD, parses current specs, computes canonical `seedProjectionSha256`, scans bundle directories only, and orders archived timestamp + change ID.
2. Historical parser validates only ID/timestamps/strict deltas needed for authority, tolerating unrelated task/report schema drift.
3. Resolve manifest or immutable legacy baseline; simulate each archive against one evolving map.
4. Report every archive `complete`, `repaired`, `conflict`, or `unreadable`, plus seed/head/digests and exact conflict bindings.
5. Execute acquires shared lock before loading state; requires reviewed seed HEAD/digest; reruns the complete simulation under lock.
6. Write only final safe targets, re-read versions/spec/doc digests, and release lock.

Undisposed conflict, unverified authority, stale seed, malformed disposition, or additional conflict causes zero writes for that archive.

## Add-only preserve-current disposition v1

Operational dry-run found parent `fixWorkflowReliabilityDefects` archived add `dl-reportDiagnostics01` for `rq-subagentReports24` differs from current shipped law introduced by parent task checkpoint `76eaad8d`. User selected preserving current law while allowing independently safe sibling deltas.

V1 supports **only `operation: add` where target requirement already exists and normal planner proves same-ID normalized-content conflict**. Modify/remove/rename are rejected as unsupported/unverified; no generic postimage inference.

Typed input:

- exact `changeId`
- exact `deltaId`
- literal `resolution: preserve_current`
- `currentRequirementSha256`
- `rejectedPostimageSha256` (canonical archived add requirement)
- non-empty evidence

Processing:

1. Under shared lock, run normal planner and prove exact row is conflicting add.
2. Compute current and rejected requirement digests with canonical codec.
3. Require exact IDs/digests plus approved execution and unchanged reviewed seed.
4. Record `preserved_current`; never write rejected postimage.
5. Exclude only that exact add and independently re-plan remaining operations from unchanged cumulative state.
6. Any other blocker aborts archive with zero writes.
7. If remaining rows are safe, apply them; preserved requirement remains byte-identical and causes no version bump by itself.
8. Output applied disposition/evidence without modifying archived bundle/history.

No wildcard, capability bypass, free-form ignore, accepted-debt path, archived overwrite, or support for modify/remove/rename exists in v1.

## Spec laws

- `rq-archiveDeltaReconciliation01`: full released projection proof before terminal success.
- `rq-archiveOrdering01`: existing-bundle retry reconciles/proves before status.
- `rq-archiveRetryIdempotence01`: cleanup no-op still requires immutable proof.
- `rq-archiveConflictDisposition01`: exact digest-bound preserve-current disposition may unlock independently safe siblings; rejected law never writes. V1 implementation is add-only; unsupported operation bindings fail closed.

## Implementation sequence

1. Existing typed planner, canonical codec, worktree archive, immutable proof, Temporal receipts, shared recovery gates.
2. Keep directory-only scanner, authority-only legacy parser, extension preservation.
3. Add shared archive-projection lock and seed-map digest; route normal and historical writers through it.
4. Add add-only disposition schema/action args, conflict diagnostics, seed binding, planner exclusion/replan, audit output.
5. Tests: stale HEAD, stale seed digest, concurrent cooperative writer, lock release, non-directory files, legacy metadata, extension preservation, exact add conflict, stale disposition digest, unsupported modify/remove/rename, second conflict, no overwrite, safe sibling recovery.
6. Re-run reviewed dry-run; capture exact parent digests/seed.
7. Planning approval authorizes exact mutation; execute and verify parent requirements, versions/docs, single-copy byte-identical rq-subagentReports24.
8. Route matrix, partial-failure retry, replay, full suite/check/build.

## Invariants

- One canonical codec owns all proof/disposition/seed hashes.
- One cooperative lock serializes every archive projection writer from seed read through readback.
- Execute is CAS-bound to reviewed dry-run HEAD and seed projection digest.
- Undisposed/stale/unsupported conflict causes zero archive writes.
- Preserve-current v1 accepts conflicting add only, exact IDs and dual digests.
- Safe siblings re-plan independently after exclusion.
- Terminal proof reads manifest/spec/docs from one immutable commit.
- Retry reaches fixed point without duplicate or rebump.
- Historical ordering/chain are deterministic and bounded.
- Parent rq-subagentReports24 remains single-copy and byte-identical.

## Validation history

Original validation attempt 1 found spec-law, duplicate Temporal writer, and chain gaps; remediated. Attempt 2 passed. Operational dry-run exposed scanner, legacy parser, extension compatibility, and real parent conflict; focused fixes/reviewer attempt 3 passed. Revised disposition validation attempt 1 found TOCTOU and undefined non-add postimage blockers. This revision adds shared lock + dry-run CAS and restricts v1 to conflicting add operations only. Independent revalidation required before planning.
